chain.label: Runway 6L ILS glideslope out of service for reconstruction
chain.trigger: NOTAMs..., runway six left ILS glideslope out of service until further notice

chain.label: High terrain at Nimitz Hill on final approach course, DME offset from airport
chain.trigger: the area where the NIMITZ VOR is located was mountainous and required extra attention (referring to this area as a "black hole")

chain.label: Approach flown during hours of darkness
chain.trigger: The accident occurred at 13° 27.35 minutes north latitude...during the hours of darkness.

chain.label: Korean Air training omitted varied nonprecision approach scenarios
chain.trigger: The countdown/count up DME/localizer procedure...was not included in any of the Korean Air simulator training scenarios

chain.label: FAA intentionally inhibited Guam MSAW inside 54 nm ring
chain.trigger: The new software was designed to inhibit MSAW alerts inside a 54-nm radius of the Guam ASR-8 site.

chain.label: Captain expected a visual approach based on familiarization video and prior trip
chain.trigger: since the visibility is six, when we are in the visual approach, as I said before, set the VOR on number two

caused_by.evidence: the presentation stated that "...you [the pilot] will be radar-vectored to ILS runway 6L.... You will then perform a visual approach."

chain.label: Captain gave abbreviated approach briefing omitting step-down fixes and altitudes
chain.trigger: I will give you a short briefing...

caused_by.evidence: the captain's expectation of a visual approach was a factor in his incomplete briefing of the localizer approach
deficiencies associated with fatigue were displayed in many aspects of the captain's behavior...his incomplete briefing

chain.label: Flight entered rain shower and IMC on final approach, no runway in sight
chain.trigger: Korean Air flight 801 encountered instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) as the flight continued on its approach

chain.label: Captain became confused and preoccupied with glideslope status
chain.trigger: About 0141:46, the captain asked, "isn't glideslope working?"

caused_by.evidence: the CVR recorded a series of conflicting flight crew comments concerning the operational status of the glideslope
by not fully briefing the instrument approach, the captain missed an opportunity to prepare himself...for the relatively complex localizer-only approach
The captain's preoccupation and confusion with the status of the glideslope to the exclusion of other critical information...typical of fatigue effects

chain.label: Captain lost positional awareness on the localizer-only approach
chain.trigger: the captain lost awareness of flight 801's position on the ILS localizer-only approach to runway 6L

caused_by.evidence: as a result of his confusion and preoccupation with the status of the glideslope, failure to properly cross-check the airplane's position and altitude
the approach progressed without encountering the visual conditions the captain had anticipated
A countdown/count up DME procedure, which is rarely encountered on a localizer procedure, was not included in any of the Korean Air simulator training scenarios

chain.label: Captain ordered premature altitude-selector resets, descending below 2,000 and 1,440 ft step-down minimums
chain.trigger: the captain directed the first officer to reset the altitude selector to 1,440 feet...before the autopilot had...reached the GUQQY outer marker/1.6 DME fix

caused_by.evidence: The captain's premature orders to reset the altitude selector indicated that he had lost awareness of the airplane's position along the final approach course.

chain.label: First officer and flight engineer failed to monitor and challenge the premature descent
chain.trigger: the first officer and flight engineer failed to properly monitor and/or challenge the captain's performance

caused_by.evidence: the captain...failed to provide the first officer and flight engineer with adequate guidance about monitoring the approach
the first officer did not challenge the captain's premature descents below 2,000 and 1,440 feet
the company had encountered difficulties teaching some first officers and flight engineers to challenge the captain and intervene in safety-of-flight situations

chain.label: CERAP controller failed to monitor the flight, issue position advisory, or relay weather
chain.trigger: the CERAP controller's performance was substandard in that he failed to provide the flight crew with a position advisory...and monitor the flight

caused_by.evidence: The ARTS IIA system recorded no alerts for Korean Air flight 801 at any time.

chain.label: Airplane descended well below approach path toward Nimitz Hill without terrain warning
chain.trigger: FDR data indicated that the airplane was descending below 2,000 feet msl at a point 6.8 nm from the runway threshold

caused_by.evidence: the autopilot continued to descend the airplane prematurely through the 2,000- and 1,440-foot intermediate altitude constraints
no change in the airplane's descent profile followed, and the CVR indicated that the flight engineer continued to complete the landing checklist
crashed into high terrain about 3 miles southwest of the airport
if the ARTS IIA MSAW system had been operating as initially intended, a visual and aural warning would have activated about 64 seconds before flight 801 impacted terrain
the controller might have seen the airplane descend prematurely toward high terrain and have been able to alert the flight crew

chain.label: Captain failed to react to GPWS callouts; missed approach initiated too late
chain.trigger: the captain's failure to react properly to the GPWS minimums callout and the direct challenge from the first officer precluded action that might have prevented the accident

caused_by.evidence: the GPWS issued a "minimums minimums" annunciation followed by a "sink rate" alert about 3 seconds later
the captain apparently became confused about the glideslope's status
his failure to react to the GPWS alerts are typical of fatigue effects

chain.label: Controlled flight into terrain at Nimitz Hill
chain.trigger: About 0142:26, the airplane impacted hilly terrain at Nimitz Hill, Guam, about 660 feet msl

chain.label: 228 killed, 26 seriously injured; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: Of the 254 persons on board, 228 were killed, and 23 passengers and 3 flight attendants survived the accident with serious injuries.

caused_by.evidence: The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire.
